text:
alex_product: Quick kickoff — we need to finalize Dedicated autoscale + SLA proposal for Q2 OKRs. Main asks: predictable baseline for committed customers, elastic burst for PLG, and tenant isolation guarantees. Who can help scope launch criteria?

maria_eng_platform: I can take the autoscale policy draft. Important tradeoff: burst pool can reduce cold-starts but complicates accounting. Need exact metrics customers expect for "reserved" vs "burst".

jess_customer_success: From customer side: enterprise customers want a firm P99 latency target for reserved capacity and an explicit statement that burst is best-effort (no SLA). Also they ask for tenant-level isolation (no noisy neighbor) and audit logs for when burst is used.

sam_sre: Agree with Jess. For Dedicated we should offer 99.9% uptime SLA on the control plane and P99 latency SLA for the RESERVED capacity only. Burst = best-effort, with rate-limited spill. Also need a mitigation policy for fallback to smaller model variant when queue fills.

kai_engineer: Draft policy snippet I tried last week (example):
```json
{
  "policy": "reserved+burst",
  "reserved_min_gpus": 2,
  "burst_pool_share_pct": 15,
  "burst_rate_limit_tps": 25,
  "sla_reserved_p99_latency_ms": 200,
  "sla_burst": "best_effort"
}
```
This is intentionally conservative. We can tune numbers after canary.

maria_eng_platform: Implementation notes: autoscaler must enforce two gates: (1) immediate reservation reclaim for reserved customers, (2) global burst budget that decays over time (leaky bucket). Also we need accounting events: burst_granted, burst_denied, reserved_reclaim. Those should be plumbed into the Console for billing/alerts.

alex_product: Good. Let's get to launch criteria. My proposal:
- Must-have: documented autoscale policy + config UI in Console for Dedicated customers.
- Must-have: SLA doc for reserved capacity (uptime + P99).
- Must-have: audit events for burst usage and isolation incidents.
- Should-have: automatic fallback to compatible model variant if latency deteriorates.
- Nice-to-have: per-tenant burst credits purchasable as add-on.

jess_customer_success: For customer acceptance tests: 1) run synthetic load showing reserved capacity meets P99 target for 24h, 2) demonstrate burst handing during 1h spike (show audit, show degraded SLO for burst), 3) show isolation test where noisy tenant doesn't affect reserved tenants. Customers will want test artifacts.

sam_sre: Risk log:
- Risk: burst pool starves reserved capacity due to bug -> mitigation: strict reclaim with soft/hard reclaim thresholds and kill-switch for burst.
- Risk: billing mismatch if burst isn't accounted -> mitigation: stream events to billing pipeline + reconcile job.

kai_engineer: Timeline ask: for Q2 beta we can deliver the autoscaler + Console toggle and basic logging in 6 weeks assuming priority. SLA legal write-up + pricing will need product & revenue review in parallel.

alex_product: Scope negotiation: If legal/product review blocks, we can ship beta with "best-effort" guidance and explicit warning, but reserve SLA for GA only. Need buy-in from Sales for messaging. Thoughts?

jess_customer_success: Sales input: They'll accept beta best-effort messaging for early customers (with credits) but top-tier customers will require contract language before any Dedicated migration. So GA SLA is critical for enterprise deals.

maria_eng_platform: Dev ops checklist for beta:
- Feature flag for burst pool (on/off per-tenant)
- Telemetry: burst_granted/denied, reserved_reclaim, queue_depth, p99_latency
- Canary rollout to internal tenants + 2 pilot customers
- Automated regression tests for reclaim behavior

alex_product: OK action items: (1) Maria + Kai produce autoscale config RFC by next Wed (1764273923). (2) Sam to draft SRE mitigation playbook. (3) Jess to line up 2 pilot customers and acceptance tests. (4) I'll coordinate legal/product for SLA language.

deploy-bot: new-canary deployed: dedicated-autoscale:v0.1 to infra-canary (1763669700)

kai_engineer: Noted. I'll start on RFC today. Quick question: for burst accounting do we tie to token usage or GPU-seconds? Token usage maps to cost but GPU-seconds is closer to capacity. Prefer GPU-seconds for fairness.

sam_sre: Use GPU-seconds for enforcement, token usage for billing conversion (post-hoc). Keep enforcement simple.

alex_product: Solid. Thanks everyone — let's aim to review the RFC in the product sync on Friday. :thumbsup:
